title: for arg in args.by_ref() is obscure; while-let-next is clearer
description: smtp/main.rs, imap/main.rs, mail/main.rs all use 'for arg in args.by_ref() { if arg == "--config" { match args.next() ... } }' to parse CLI args. The by_ref() borrow is needed so the for-loop and the inner args.next() share the same iterator state. This is correct but unfamiliar: most Rust readers encountering by_ref() inside a for loop have to pause and think. The standard idiomatic pattern for this problem is 'while let Some(arg) = args.next() { if arg == "--config" { let path = args.next().ok_or_else(|| ...); } }' which makes the shared iterator state obvious. All three binaries copy-paste the same parse_args() — they could share a single implementation in a common module, reducing the surface where this pattern needs to be understood.
